disagreements.topic: Google default-search payment: tail risk or in-horizon risk
disagreements.positions: Agent 2 keeps extra left-tail weight because DOJ's cross-appeal explicitly asks the D.C. Circuit to ban Google's payments to distributors, with a ruling likely by mid-2027. Agents 1, 3, 4 and 5 treat it as a late-horizon tail, since current remedies allow non-exclusive payments.
disagreements.resolution: Both are partly right. DOJ's cross-appeal does seek to vacate the denial of a payment ban, so the risk is more than hypothetical, as agent 2 says. But oral argument is still unscheduled, Google's reply brief is due 2026-09-29, and analysts expect argument in late 2026 or early 2027 with a ruling not before 2027. A ruling that imposes a ban and takes effect before 2027-09-25 is a low-probability event, perhaps 5-10%. It would hit a ~$20B/yr, nearly all-margin revenue line (roughly 10-15% of EPS). The revised mean already carries this in its left tail, so I make no further change.
disagreements.evidence: DOJ response and cross-appeal brief (Nos. 26-5023/5047/5049, 'oral argument not yet scheduled'); Courthouse News, July 2026; 9to5Mac 2026-02-03.

disagreements.topic: How far the rate regime should pull the median below spot
disagreements.positions: In round 2 all five agents moved their medians to ~$332-337, i.e. 1-3% below the $341 spot. P(>=341) now ranges 0.465-0.48, with a mean of 0.474, below the round-1 supervisor's own 0.49. Their fair values of $312-320 assume a de-rating to ~30-30.5x because the Fed is 'hiking' against a 5%+ 10-year.
disagreements.resolution: The facts on rates hold, but the forward path is less hawkish than 'a hiking cycle' suggests. The September SEP median has one more 25bp hike to ~4.10% by end-2026 and then no further hikes in 2027. The 10-year closed 2026-09-25 at ~5.17% (5.18% was the 9/24 intraday/close high), i.e. the stock already prices a post-2007 high yield. Agents' blended fair values therefore embed de-rating that the $341 close has largely discounted. The round-2 herd moved past what the evidence supports. I nudge the center back up ~1.5pts, to roughly where the round-1 supervisor put it, while keeping the fatter left tail.
disagreements.evidence: Fed September 2026 SEP/dot plot coverage (Raisin, Bondsavvy, Schwab): 2026 median 4.10%, flat through 2027, core PCE 3.4%; CNBC 2026-09-25: 10-year little changed at ~5.163% after its highest level since June 2007 on Thursday.

disagreements.positions: Agents 2 and 4 include DCFs at $280 and $265 (8.0-8.5% discount rates), weighted 20-25%. Agents 1, 3 and 5 use only P/E and FCF yield ($312-334). Fair values: 315, 312, 320, 312, 320.
disagreements.resolution: The DCFs mostly restate the discount-rate assumption (agent 2 gets $318 at 7.5%), not new fundamentals. They are useful as a signal of rate sensitivity but should not drag fair value much below ~$315. P/E on FY28 EPS (~$10.3-10.4 x 30.5x = ~$315) and FCF yield (~$316-334) cluster tightly. I reconcile fair value at ~$318.
disagreements.evidence: Agents' own method inputs; Apple 8-K FQ3 FY2026 (9M diluted EPS $6.88) for the FY26 ~$8.86 base all agents now share.

disagreements.positions: Agent 4 holds $240, arguing a de-rating into the mid-$250s is ordinary multiple risk in a hiking cycle. Agents 1, 2, 3 and 5 are at $250-252.
disagreements.resolution: The Fed's projected peak near 4.10% limits how far a pure rate de-rating runs. ~28-29x on ~$10 NTM EPS is ~$280-290, and a close below ~$250 (~26x FY27E, near the $243 52-week low) requires estimate cuts. I set the break at $248, close to the agents' mean.

disagreements.positions: All agents now include the 2027-06-23 step-up. Agents 4 and 5 put a 'punitive' rate in their bear cases.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed: USTR's final Section 301 action sets 0% until 2027-06-23, then a rate to be announced at least 30 days before that date. It targets foundational/legacy-node Chinese semiconductors, including those embedded in downstream products. Apple's direct exposure is to legacy components in China-assembled devices, not its TSMC-made SoCs, so it is a moderate, not severe, risk. It is also a bargaining chip that may be moderated. It is correctly weighted as a small left-tail item.
disagreements.evidence: USTR Section 301 final action FRN (2025-12-22); CNBC 2025-12-23; Sheppard Mullin 'Blank slate or bargaining chip'.

fair_value.method: No-DCF rule (Kilian 2026-10-21 13:50Z: no DCF leg for any researched name except the neoclouds), applied 2026-10-22: drops the 0.1 DCF leg ($300): (0.55 x 316 + 0.35 x 324) / 0.9 = $319.11 (was $318.0; other legs renormalised, nothing else changed). Original: Reconciled from the five revised forecasts: forward P/E and FCF yield on FY28 figures, with DCFs used only as a rate-sensitivity check. The forecast median (~$338) sits above fair value because the 5.17% 10-year is already in the $341 close, the Fed projects a peak near 4.10% with no 2027 hikes, and product-cycle momentum plus ~2.5%/yr buybacks rarely let a mega-cap converge fully to a static fair value within 12 months.

methods.name: Forward P/E on FY28 EPS
methods.assumptions: FY26 ~$8.86 (9M $6.88 + ~$1.98 FQ4), FY27 consensus ~$9.58 (+8%), FY28 ~$10.35 (+8%; price increases offset 2027 DRAM at ~$2.00/Gb, no memory relief before 2028) x 30.5x (the agents' consensus multiple: a premium to the ~27-30x five-year band, but de-rated from ~35.6x for 5%+ Treasuries).

methods.name: FCF yield on FY28 FCF/share
methods.assumptions: FY28 FCF ~$135-147B on ~14.1-14.3B shares = ~$9.7-10.4/share at a 3.0-3.2% required yield; the midpoint of agents 1, 3, 4 and 5 ($320, $325, $334, $316).

methods.name: DCF (rate-sensitivity check)
methods.assumptions: Agents 2 and 4: $280 at 8.0% and $265 at 8.5% WACC, $318 at 7.5%. Midpoint ~$300; low weight because the result mostly restates the discount-rate choice.

methods.name: Street consensus target (cross-check only)
methods.assumptions: Mean target ~$328 (Morgan Stanley $360, BofA $370 after a memory-driven cut); evidence, not blended.

changes.why: The Fed's September SEP shows one more hike to ~4.10% and then a hold through 2027, and the 5.17% 10-year is already in the price. All five agents moved below the round-1 supervisor's own 0.49 in round 2, which looks like herding past the evidence rather than new information.
The same ~1-1.5pt upward shift of the center (median ~$333 to ~$338), with dispersion unchanged at ~27% log-vol.
The fat left tail (Google payment-ban cross-appeal, 2027-06-23 China chip-tariff step-up, memory outrunning pricing) is confirmed by the searches and kept.
DCF inputs are down-weighted because they mainly restate discount-rate choices; P/E and FCF-yield methods cluster at $316-324.
Essentially the mean. A Fed peak near 4.10% limits pure de-rating to ~$280-290, so a close below ~$248 (~26x FY27E, near the $243 52-week low) signals estimate cuts.

confidence_reason: The revised forecasters have converged tightly (P(>=341) 0.465-0.48), and my searches mostly confirmed their facts: the payment-ban cross-appeal is real but a ruling before 2027 is unlikely, and the June 2027 tariff rate is TBA. The only point pushing back toward spot is that the Fed projects a peak near 4.10% with no 2027 hikes and the 5.17% 10-year is already priced. That argues the round-2 move below the round-1 supervisor's 0.49 overshot, but it is a judgment about how much is priced in, not a settled factual disagreement. So the update is small and low-confidence.
thesis_break_reason: About -27% from $341, just above the $243 52-week low and ~26x FY27 consensus EPS of ~$9.58. With the Fed projecting a peak near 4.10% and a flat 2027 path, rate-driven de-rating to ~28-29x on intact ~$10 NTM EPS reaches roughly $280-290 without breaking the thesis. A close below ~$248 would mean earnings estimates are being cut. Likely causes: gross margin guided well below 46% as ~$2.00/Gb DRAM outruns price increases, iPhone 18/Duo unit declines after the price hikes, a D.C. Circuit ruling that bans Google's distributor payments (~$20B/yr), or a punitive China semiconductor tariff rate on 2027-06-23.
key_drivers: Valuation vs rates: ~35.6x FY27 EPS for ~8% EPS growth (FY26 ~$8.86 to FY27 ~$9.58), with the 10-year at 5.17% (highest since 2007). The Fed SEP sees one more hike to ~4.10% and then a hold through 2027, with core PCE at 3.4%.
Memory costs: 2027 DRAM contracted at ~$2.00/Gb vs $1.50 (+33%), no relief before 2028. Margins (FQ4 guide 47-48% vs 50.1%) depend on price increases, not cost relief.

Product cycle: record close ~$344.70 (2026-09-22, $5T market cap) on iPhone 18 Pro lead times, the ~$1,999 Duo (Morgan Stanley: ~$14B December-quarter revenue) and Gemini-based Siri. FQ4 results ~2026-10-29.

Google payments: DOJ cross-appeal seeks a payment ban. Oral argument is unscheduled, Google's reply brief is due 2026-09-29, and a ruling is not expected before 2027. A low-probability, high-impact in-horizon tail.
China chip tariff: the Section 301 rate on Chinese legacy semiconductors steps up from 0% on 2027-06-23, with the rate announced at least 30 days before.
summary: After round 2 the five forecasters agree closely: fair value ~$312-320, median ~$333, P(close >= $341 on 2027-09-25) ~0.47, all driven by a 5%+ 10-year, 2027 memory costs locked ~33% higher, and only ~8% EPS growth against a ~35.6x multiple. My checks confirmed those facts and the tails (DOJ's payment-ban cross-appeal, the June 2027 China chip-tariff step-up). They also showed the Fed projecting a peak near 4.10% with no 2027 hikes, with the 5.17% yield already in the $341 price. I therefore nudge the center back up slightly: median ~$338, P(>=341) ~0.49, fair value $318, thesis break $248. This is a low-confidence adjustment, so the forecasters' mean remains a sound baseline.
